description: RL-AERPAW-DT is a UAV communications digital-twin environment developed by Everett Tucker and Yuchen Liu at North Carolina State University. It combines Sionna ray tracing, three-dimensional building scenes and ground-user trajectories to compute radio maps and examine UAV positions and user association. The README describes importing building geometry through Blender/Mitsuba and mobility traces from SUMO. Its sample coverage is a Raleigh urban scenario and Python library and notebook interfaces. Outputs include path gain, received signal strength and SINR maps. The provider identifies communication optimisation and task planning as applications. Access is through a public GitHub repository; no licence was identified, so reuse permission remains uncertain. The README specifies Linux support and Sionna version dependencies. Its reinforcement-learning control pipeline is listed as ongoing work; the title does not establish a completed learning controller. Related AERPAW measurement collections provide separate calibration observations. The software was not installed or executed.
